chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about one performing tamattuʿ who arrives in Makkah on the night of ʿArafah. He said: There is no tamattuʿ for him; he makes it into an individual hajj, performs tawaf of the House, goes between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and goes out to Mina. There is no sacrificial offering upon him; rather, the sacrificial offering is only upon the one performing tamattuʿ.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: the first of the two hills between which saʿy is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: the second of the two hills between which saʿy is performed
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: the sacrificial offering associated here with hajj al-tamattuʿ
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: the Kaʿbah, around which tawaf is performed
key_terms.حَجَّةً مُفْرَدَةً: an individual hajj rite not joined with ʿumrah as tamattuʿ
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: the night before the standing of ʿArafah, marking a critical hajj time limit
key_terms.مِنًى: the hajj site to which the pilgrim proceeds for the rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone intending hajj al-tamattuʿ who arrives in Makkah on the night of ʿArafah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the pilgrim intending hajj al-tamattuʿ who reaches Makkah too late, on the night of ʿArafah. In that case, his tamattuʿ no longer applies, and he converts his rite into hajj al-ifrad, performing tawaf and saʿy without the obligation of hady. The narration clarifies that the sacrificial offering is specifically required for the pilgrim properly performing tamattuʿ.
